text: Every job run writes history automatically. Before checking permissions or assuming anything, look at what actually happened — the message column usually contains the real error, verbatim.
A job with five steps failing tells you almost nothing on its own. The step_id in the history tells you exactly which one, and what to test manually outside of Agent, as the same account Agent uses.

This is the cause that catches DBAs who assume the T-SQL is the problem when it isn't. A CmdExec or PowerShell step runs as the Agent service account by default, not your login — a dedicated proxy account scoped to what the step needs is the correct fix.
Schedule conflicts between jobs, a dependent resource not ready yet, and context differences between running something manually in SSMS versus under the job owner's actual permissions.
Job history first, isolate the step, check the account it actually ran as. Next up: automating DBA maintenance.
